BiblicalUsage: A sweet savour is the pleasure of the sacrifice, and the kings' decrees use the word for it. Darius orders sacrifices of sweet savours to the God of heaven, and Nebuchadnezzar, after the dream is told, commands sweet odours to be offered to Daniel himself — the same pleasure, aimed at the wrong person.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sweet savour belongs to God alone: the king offers it rightly to heaven, and wrongly to a man.
